[S514] Leo Carrington [V158] [3399]: Thank you very much. [S515] Good morning. [S516] Just one follow-up from me. [S517] If you could elaborate, please, on the points you made on tariffs. [S518] I think you probably were focusing more on the uniforms and rental costs, but have you seen any effects on your cost base in terms of CapEx. [S519] Any changes to your CapEx expectations? [S520] Thank you.
[S521] Todd Schneider [V159] [3423]: Yes. [S522] Thank you, Leo, for the question. [S523] You know, the tariffs are, as I mentioned, we're not immune from them. [S524] But our supply chain organization supports our entire business, not just our rental business. [S525] And they're doing a great job. [S526] So, you know, when I talk about a great job, all those items of You know, the geographic diversity, the having optionality with all the different providers, that applies to each of our businesses. [S527] And as a result, you know, we're finding ways to become more efficient. [S528] So that culture is shining through. [S529] And when you go through really challenging times, like what tariffs throw at you, it gives our organization opportunity to shine. [S530] And our supply chain is doing just that. [S531] And they're continuing to fight through what is a challenging environment. [S532] From a CapEx standpoint, our [V160] 4% targeted CapEx, I think you'll see that be consistent. [S533] We would expect that that would be where we plan to be moving forward.
